"''And neither will the Rebellion.|Hera Syndulla and Kanan Jarrus|}} The '''TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter''', also called the '''TIE/D Defender''' or simply the '''TIE Defender''', was an advanced experimental [[TIE series]] [[starfighter]] manufactured by [[Sienar Fleet Systems]] for the [[Imperial Navy]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. The starfighter was referred to as the '''TIE Defender project''' or the '''TIE Defender program''' while under development. Unlike previous [[Twin ion engine|TIE]] models, the starfighter featured a [[hyperdrive]] as well as [[deflector shield]]s, and was easily recognized by its three wings mounted around an aft section of the [[cockpit]]. These specifications made the fighter much more difficult to destroy than standard [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]]. The TIE Defender was considered a fighter-[[bomber]]; it was armed with heavy [[cannon]]s and [[missile]]s. The ship was designed by [[Morgan Elsbeth]] and introduced as a result of [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]]'s new fighter initiative at the [[Imperial Armory Complex|Imperial Factory]] on [[Lothal]] in the [[Standard year|year]] [[2 BBY]], launched to deal with the growing rebel threat. It was supported by both [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] and [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Palpatine]]. It was developed from a prototype called the [[TIE Advanced x7]]. As the project was to be less expensive than [[Project Stardust]], and due to the constant delays of [[Director]] [[Orson Callan Krennic]], many in the Empire started to consider using the fundings of Project Stardust for Thrawn's TIE/D Defender instead. However, after [[Governor]] [[Arihnda Pryce]] destroyed Lothal's fuel depot to kill [[Jedi Knight]] [[Kanan Jarrus]], the project was halted indefinitely. Additionally, the funding for the fighter line was ultimately reassigned for Project Stardust. Although it never saw widespread use during the [[Galactic Civil War]], many of its design features were later incorporated into the [[TIE/sf space superiority fighter]] and [[TIE/vn space superiority fighter]] of the [[First Order]], the Empire's successor. ==Characteristics== {{Quote|Get out of there, both of you. I know that ship. It's a prototype TIE Defender. It's armed with heavy cannons and shields.|Ezra Bridger|}} [[File:TIED_Defender_Schematics-SW_Rebels-An_Inside_Man.png|thumb|left|220px|TIE/D Defender schematics]] Like the rest of the [[TIE series|TIE fighter series]] [[starfighter]]s,''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' the TIE/D Defender featured a ball-shaped [[cockpit]] module and [[Solar collector|solar array]] wings. However, while the standard [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]] and many other [[Twin ion engine|TIE]] variants, including the [[TIE/IN interceptor]] and the [[TIE Advanced x1]], had two parallel wings to either side of the [[pilot]] module, the TIE/D Defender had three wings mounted around an aft section of the [[cockpit]]. It also included [[deflector shield]]s and a [[hyperdrive]], new features for TIE fighters. The fighters [[P-sz9.7 twin ion engine]]s were too fast for [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber|Y-wing starfighters]] and armed with six [[L-s9.3 laser cannon]]s, [[CLL-3 Ion Torpedo]]es, and [[concussion missile]]s—causing high damage over a moderate area. [[TIE/D Defender Elite|Some TIE/Ds]] featured six additional [[missile]]s and [[Color|red]] markings on their wings, similar to some elite TIE [[interceptor]]s.{{Rebels|The Antilles Extraction}} As development of the TIE Defender progressed, a new variant was produced, which was classified as the TIE Defender Elite, with the faster and stronger prototype being tested by [[Commander]] [[Vult Skerris]]. The speed and maneuverability of this craft was drastically increased compared to the earlier Defender prototypes, along with stronger shields, better hyperdrive, and the addition of six missiles mounted onto the wings. ==History== ===Thrawn's new initiative=== {{Quote|A new fighter? Difficult to see how one small ship will change much.''"
"''Agent, victory and defeat are often determined by the smallest detail.|[[Imperial Security Bureau|ISB]] [[Agent]] [[Alexsandr Kallus]] and Grand Admiral Thrawn|}}
[[File:Spectres_discover_TIE_Defender.jpg|thumb|240px|The rebels examine the stolen TIE/D Defender schematics.]]
The designs of the TIE Defender were first drafted by [[Morgan Elsbeth]], who attempted to convince various Imperial officers during a presentation on [[Coruscant]] of its benefits. However, [[Moff]] [[Isdain]] bluntly rejected the offer due to its great costs. In the [[Standard year|year]] [[2 BBY]], the [[Galactic Empire]], at the instigation of [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]], began preparations to mass produce TIE Defenders at the [[Imperial Armory Complex|Imperial Factory]] on the [[planet]] [[Lothal]]. With the help of [[Ryder Azadi]]'s [[Lothal resistance group]], the [[Spectres]] [[Infiltration of the Imperial Armory Complex|stole]] the starfighter's schematics. Upon seeing the Defender's specifications, [[Captain]] [[Hera Syndulla]] of [[Phoenix Cell]] feared that if the Empire were to mass produce them, their [[Rebel pilot|pilots]] wouldn't have a chance against them. According to some accounts from the [[Sienar Advanced Projects Laboratory]], Thrawn showed the designers a rare [[Kamino saberdart]] to convey several of his proposals for aspects of the Defender. The saberdart showcased the proposed shape and positions of the Defender's wings, as well as the "unparalleled" visibility and heightened maneuverability the design would grant its pilots. Thrawn's project was supported by high-ranking Imperial officials, such as [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] and Grand Admiral [[Balanhai Savit]] as well as [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Palpatine]] himself.''[[Thrawn: Treason]]'' Although most of the Empire's R&D funding was tied up in [[Project Stardust]], supervised by [[Director]] [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]], Tarkin and other Imperial leaders had become dissatisfied with its progress, which had turned into a costly operation without yielding any results. This allowed Thrawn, backed by the disgruntled Tarkin, who was a rival to Krennic, to acquire the funding necessary to begin production of the TIE Defender on Lothal.{{Rebels|Jedi Night}}''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' ===Chasing Mon Mothma=== {{Dialogue|Kassius Konstantine|Through the nebula?|Arihnda Pryce|Our capital ships can't follow her.|Thrawn|Precisely. So I've readied my new prototype and our best pilot to hunt down and capture this rogue senator.|attr=Admiral Konstantine, Governor Pryce and Grand Admiral Thrawn on planning to capture Senator Mon Mothma|src=}} [[File:Nebula_fight.jpg|thumb|left|240px|The TIE/D Defender firing at the rebel ships in the Archeon Nebula.]] Thrawn's fighter initiative was able to produce a prototype for the TIE Defender in a short amount of [[time]], and it was first used during a [[Operation Handoff|mission]] to capture the rebel [[senator]] [[Mon Mothma]]. The ''[[Ghost]]'' crew [[transport]]ed the senator through the [[Archeon Nebula]] to avoid Imperial [[capital ship]]s. Thrawn then tasked the [[Imperial Starfighter Pilot|TIE fighter pilot]] Vult Skerris to pilot the prototype and flush the rebels out into the open, with the assistance of two TIE Interceptors. The experimental fighter proved to be very effective against the rebel pilots, as Skerris easily destroyed three [[BTL Y-wing starfighter|Y-wing starfighters]] of [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]]. The rebels then attempted to defeat Skerris by getting close to a forming [[star]] in the [[nebula]], but the ship was able to withstand the extreme [[temperature]] which burned up the TIE Interceptors. Eventually, the rebel pilots [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Ezra Bridger]] and [[Captain]] [[Jon Vander|Jon "Dutch" Vander]] managed to disable the prototype by hitting the ship with an [[ion cannon]] before making their escape. Despite the failed mission, the mission was seen as a relatively successful test of the new ship. ===Vader's support=== {{Quote|The Defender is an excellent ship. I will speak to the Emperor on behalf of the project. But it needs to be faster, and more heavily armed. The controls, too, should also be made simpler.|Darth Vader|''[[Thrawn: Alliances]]''}} [[File:DarthVader-SASP.png|thumb|right|250px|Darth Vader piloting a TIE Defender]] Defenders were used by the Seventh Fleet and eventually [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] himself after he, Thrawn, and the fleet engaged in a [[Imperial–Grysk conflict|conflict]] against the [[Grysk Hegemony]]. After completing their mission, Vader spoke to Thrawn about the Defender. He informed Thrawn that he believed the Defender was an excellent ship and that he would speak to the Emperor on behalf of the project. Vader informed Thrawn that the ship, however, needed to be faster and more heavily armed than it currently was. The ship's controls also needed to be simpler to handle. Thrawn thanked Vader for his input and assured him that he would relay the Sith Lord's recommendations to the facility on Lothal once they had returned to [[Coruscant]]. ===A new prototype=== {{Quote|My contacts tell me this new prototype is even tougher than the one you've already encountered. More powerful engines. Upgraded targeting computer.|[[Ryder Azadi]]|}} [[File:VultSkerris-SWZ84.png|thumb|left|220px|Vult Skerris's TIE Defender Elite]] Later, a new prototype, the [[TIE/D Defender Elite]], was produced on Lothal,{{Rebels|The Occupation}} adding Vader's recommendations. This model had superior speed, maneuverability, shields, and weapons. One TIE Defender Elite was [[Theft of the TIE Defender Elite|stolen]] by members of the Spectres, who had recently returned to Lothal. Thrawn activated the TIE's [[kill switch]], causing the ship to crash, however the Spectres were able to salvage the ship's hyperdrive and [[flight data recorder]]. Eventually, the flight data recorder made its way to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] and they decided to launch an [[attack on Lothal]].{{Rebels|Crawler Commandeers}} In the ensuing battle, another TIE Defender Elite was used by Skerris, but was shot down by the rebels and crashed into a [[Arquitens-class command cruiser|''Arquitens''-class command cruiser]], which in turn crashed into the [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] tower of an [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]].{{Rebels|Rebel Assault}} ===Project in peril=== {{Quote|Your TIE Defender program is at risk. Orson Krennic has been quite persuasive about diverting the funding to his own project: Stardust.''"
"''The Emperor has assured me that he supports my project.''"
"''In my view, Director Krennic's project has been nothing but expenses and excuses for years on end. If construction of the Defender is to continue, you must make your case directly to the Emperor himself. I have already arranged the meeting.''"
"''I'll leave immediately, Moff Tarkin.|Grand Moff Tarkin and Grand Admiral Thrawn discuss the continued support for the TIE Defender program|}} [[File:Vessery_Defender-XWMG.jpg|thumb|right|220px|A TIE Defender flying close to the surface of a star.]] With Skerris's death, [[Benj Dobbs]] was promoted to serve as commander of Thrawn's Defender squadron. After the failed attack on Lothal and the capture of [[General]] [[Hera Syndulla]], Tarkin contacted Thrawn, telling him that Krennic had been arguing strongly in favor of his project and that the TIE Defender program's funding was at risk of being pulled away to fund the continued construction of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]]. In order to persuade the Emperor to continue supporting the TIE Defender, Tarkin arranged a meeting with the Emperor for Thrawn, who immediately departed Lothal for Coruscant. Soon after his departure, a [[Rescue of Hera Syndulla (Lothal)|rescue]] of Syndulla was attempted by the remaining rebels on the planet. Although [[Governor of the Lothal sector|Governor of Lothal]] [[Arihnda Pryce]] was successful in cornering the rebels as they made their escape through the [[factory]]'s [[Lothal City fuel depot|fuel depot]], her determination to stop them led her to order the destruction of the depot. The resulting explosion resulted in the death of rebel leader and [[Jedi Knight]] [[Kanan Jarrus]], dealing a crippling blow to the rebels but an even bigger one to the Empire. With the fuel depot destroyed, the factory was instantly shut down and production of the TIE/D Defenders was brought to an indefinite halt. Thrawn was notably displeased with Pryce's actions, telling her that he will deal with her upon his return to Lothal.{{Rebels|DUME}} It was decreed that funding for the TIE Defender project would be shifted to the Death Star instead. Nevertheless, Tarkin promised that, after the completion of the superweapon, the Empire could restore funding to the Defender. However, shortly later during the [[Liberation of Lothal]], Thrawn was taken out of galactic affairs by Bridger, who summoned a pod of [[Purrgil]] to take the ''Chimaera''{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}} away to deep space. Additionally, the Death Star would be destroyed in the [[Battle of Yavin]], necessitating the construction of a [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second battle station]].''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' All the while, the TIE Defender program came to its end. Albeit with some apparent exceptions, remaining Defenders were decommissioned.[[Bounty Hunters 19|''Bounty Hunters'' 19]] ===Galactic Civil War=== [[File:Starship_Graveyard_Jakku_SWDA.png|thumb|left|225px|The wreck of a TIE Defender]] Despite the end of the program, the TIE Defender would still see some use throughout the further Galactic Civil War. The fighters were available to Captain [[Kosh]] of the [[68th Legion]]. Following the [[Attack on the Executor|battle]] at [[Jekara]],[[Bounty Hunters 18|''Bounty Hunters'' 18]] several TIE Defenders were used by [[Dark Squadron]] under bounty hunter [[Beilert Valance]]. On the order of Vader, the squadron used their defenders to [[Assassination of Tarl Sokoli|take out]] Admiral [[Tarl Sokoli]] aboard the [[Forerunner II|''Forerunner'' II]]. The appearance of Defenders came as a surprise to Sokoli, who knew their program had been decommissioned years prior. At least one Defender flew during the [[Battle of Jakku]] and was destroyed, crashing into the [[Starship Graveyard|Graveyard of Giants]]. ===Legacy=== A customised TIE/D was used by [[Kiza]], a former member of the [[Acolytes of the Beyond]],''[[Shadow of the Sith]]'' in [[21 ABY]]''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Shadow of the Sith]]'' to [[21 ABY]]. during her [[Quest for Exegol|hunt]] to find [[Exegol]]. Although the TIE/D never saw widespread use during the [[Galactic Civil War]], its nature was revived by [[First Order]] tacticians who saw it as a versatile attack craft to throw at [[New Republic]] forces. Many of its features were incorporated into the [[TIE/sf space superiority fighter]], which were later refined in the [[TIE/vn space superiority fighter]]. In addition to using the Defenders' features in the TIE/sf and TIE/vn models, First Order officials revived the Imperial TIE Defender program and regarded the TIE/D as a versatile attack craft. Further more, the TIE Defender's hybrid nature as a fighter-bomber influenced the design of [[Kylo Ren's TIE silencer]]. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|For those of us who remember playing the ''TIE Fighter'' game, it's a great ship. It's fast, it's got shields, it's got a hyperdrive. It sort of evens the odds and you don't need hundreds and hundreds upon them to defeat just a small number of Rebel starfighters. It evens the odds between the versatility of an X-wing fighter and the limited capabilities of a TIE fighter.|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|{{RebelsRecon|dRcc48GmXd0|#3.09: Inside "An Inside Man" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/rebels-recon-inside-an-inside-man}}}} [[File:TIE_Defender_concept.jpg|thumb|right|250px|TIE/D Defender concept art for ''Star Wars Rebels''.]] The TIE/D Defender originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']] by [[LucasArts]], where it was depicted as the top-of-the-line Imperial fighter model,[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']] released in [[July]] [[1994]].{{LucasArts|url=20th/history_2.htm|text=20th Anniversary History, Part Two: The Classics, 1990 - 1994}} The fighter was incorporated into [[canon]] upon its inclusion in the mobile strategy game ''[[Star Wars: Commander]]'' in late [[November]] [[2014]].{{WebCite|url=http://www.ign.com/wikis/star-wars-commander|text=Star Wars: Commander Wiki Guide|work=[http://www.ign.com IGN]|archivedate=20160823130815}} Additionally, it was later included in the ''[[Star Wars Battlefront]]'' video game as a vehicle power-up, along with the release of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] expansion pack.{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/welcome-to-the-death-star|text=Welcome to the Death Star|date=2016-09-19|nolive=1}} The TIE Defender was also featured in the [[Star Wars Rebels Season Three|third season]] of ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' animated television series, as the fighter's schematics appeared in "[[An Inside Man]]" (the tenth episode),{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/an-inside-man-episode-guide|text="An Inside Man" Episode Guide | Star Wars Rebels}} and the fighter itself later appeared in "[[Secret Cargo]]" (the eighteenth episode).{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/secret-cargo-episode-guide|text="Secret Cargo" Episode Guide | Star Wars Rebels}} According to the ''Rebels'' crew, the Defender had seemed a philosophical departure for the Empire, pouring such resources into a small fighter craft, but with a rather unconventional Imperial like Thrawn backing the project, it made sense for them to introduce the fighter into the show.{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/an-inside-man-trivia-gallery|text="An Inside Man" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|image 4 of 4}} ===Inconsistencies=== The reference book ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia of Starfighters and Other Vehicles]]'', authored by as well as its [[Star Wars Encyclopedia of Starfighters and Other Vehicles (second edition)|updated second edition]] states the TIE Defender as the first TIE series starfighter to have a hyperdrive and deflector shields;" , the [[TIE/ad v1]] and the [[TIE Advanced x1]] had them before. The former source also asserts that the TIE Defender was utilised "only against a [[Spectres|small rebel cell]] led by Hera Syndulla", of which has been conveyed to be not the case in subsequent media. ''[[TIE Fighter Owners' Workshop Manual]]'' denotes the weapons mounted onto the cockpit as laser cannons, while these are the warhead/missile launchers as proved by the ''Encyclopedia of Starfighters and Other Vehicles'' and the ''Manual's'' texts themselves. ''[[Starships and Speeders]]'' incorrectly identifies the cost of the vessel as 75,000 credits. The [[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 48|forty-eight]] issue of [[De Agostini]]'s ''[[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon]]'' incorrectly states that the vessel was developed as a response to the rebel victory at the [[Battle of Yavin]], was the first TIE series vessel to have shielding and a hyperdrive, and had it had a speed value of 144 [[megalight per hour|MGLT]]. ==Appearances==
